lines.name: Bridge Bypass Line

segments.routing: Open-lake crossing (~3.2 nm) between the SR-520 and I-90 bridges — no bridge crossing on this leg. 7-kn/100-yd Seattle shore buffer off Leschi (SMC 16.20.130); 8-mph/100-yd King County buffer (KCC 12.44.090) plus the 7-kn/300-ft swim/dock buffer inside Meydenbauer Bay on the Bellevue approach. Mid-lake is unrestricted.

lines.phase_notes: Flagship — 'the I-90/SR-520 bridge bypass.' ~12–15 min indicative including shore-buffer legs, vs a 51-min SR-520 planning time and the state's highest tolls. Both landings are real, existing public moorage — zero new infrastructure at launch. Candid: reverse flow Bellevue→Leschi is thin; this line lives or dies on Bellevue-bound seat blocks (Amazon Bellevue is 15–20 min uphill — sell honestly as longer walk / shuttle-tier).

lines.name: Boeing Line

segments.routing: ~3 nm south along the Eastside shore; cross the SR-520 floating bridge at its navigable elevated span (verify span location against chart); 100-yd shore buffers at each end; 7-kn/300-ft buffer inside Meydenbauer Bay.

South via the East Channel between Mercer Island and the Bellevue/Newcastle shore; pass the fixed I-90 East Channel bridge through its navigation span (verify against chart); Mercer Island Marine Patrol speed buoys ~300 ft offshore (8 mph/no-wake inside them); Renton 8-kn/100-yd buffer + no-wake within 100 yd of shore/bridges (RMC 9-3-7) on the Coulon approach.

lines.phase_notes: ~25–30 min end-to-end indicative (Kirkland↔Meydenbauer ~12 min; Meydenbauer↔Coulon ~20–25 min), all including buffer legs. Anchor: Boeing Renton 737 plant + Southport Office Campus — genuinely walk-tier waterfront. Kirkland's codified commercial tour-boat berth (KMC 14.36.200) makes this the easiest permit in the lake cluster.

lines.phase_notes: Phase 2 — launches once Phase 1 proves demand. Kirkland↔Leschi direct ~15–18 min indicative; Carillon Point is the inventory's infill stop and the Microsoft Redmond shuttle gate (ground shuttle, ~3.5 mi — never a water path, never implied as a Microsoft dock).

copy.hero_headline: Two floating bridges. One lake. Zero water commute — until now.
copy.hero_sub: Two floating bridges. One lake. Zero water commute — until now. Navier is building an employer water network for Seattle: 20-seat electric hydrofoils crossing Lake Washington — Leschi to Bellevue in 12–15 minutes, Kirkland and Renton linked through Meydenbauer Bay — plus a second network on Elliott Bay connecting West Seattle, the downtown waterfront, and the Expedia campus, growing to Bainbridge Island and Des Moines.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · first service no earlier than end-2027 · two independent networks (no Ship Canal / Locks connector)
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: The bridges are the bottleneck. The lake is open water.
copy.problem_lead: This region already commutes by water: Washington State Ferries' Bainbridge run is a daily 35-minute workhorse, Kitsap's fast ferries carried more than 850,000 riders in 2024, and the King County Water Taxi tops 700,000 boardings a year. Yet Lake Washington — ringed by jobs on both shores — has no scheduled water service at all. Its only crossings are two congested floating bridges, with peak SR-520 tolls of $4.90–$6.90 and a 51-minute planning time for a trip the water covers in about 15. The lake is open, legal, fast water; it just has no boats.

problem_chips.label: SR-520 planning time for the same trip
Lake Washington and Elliott Bay stay independent

copy.precedent: WSF Bainbridge, Kitsap Fast Ferries (850,000+ riders in 2024), and King County Water Taxi (700,000+ boardings/year) already prove the water works. Lake Washington has the jobs and open water — but no scheduled commute service yet.
copy.stripe_lesson: First employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. Seattle already proved the water on the Sound — we open the lake.

copy.proof_worked_body: WSF, Kitsap Fast Ferries, and King County Water Taxi move hundreds of thousands of riders a year. We complement them with employer seats and lake landings they don't serve.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — twenty-seat class is the product.

copy.network_lead: Two launch lines meet at Meydenbauer Bay: the Bridge Bypass Line (Leschi ↔ Bellevue, 12–15 min indicative — the I-90/SR-520 bypass) and the Boeing Line (Kirkland ↔ Meydenbauer Bay ↔ Renton, ~25–30 min end-to-end, landing at the walk-tier waterfront doorstep of Boeing Renton and the Southport offices). Downtown Bellevue and Amazon's Bellevue towers are a 15–20 minute uphill walk or a short shuttle from the Meydenbauer dock. Phase 2 adds a Kirkland ↔ Leschi direct (15–18 min indicative) with a Carillon Point stop and a shuttle connection toward Microsoft Redmond. The lake and the Sound operate as two independent networks. The only water between them runs through the Ballard Locks — a first-come lock queue, not a commuter connection — so we don't pretend there's a boat from Bellevue to Bainbridge. There isn't, and there won't be.
copy.network_footnote: The lake and the Sound operate as two independent networks. The only water between them runs through the Ballard Locks — a first-come lock queue, not a commuter connection — so we don't pretend there's a boat from Bellevue to Bainbridge. There isn't, and there won't be. On Elliott Bay, the Expedia Shuttle links West Seattle (Seacrest), the downtown waterfront at Bell Harbor Pier 66, and Elliott Bay Marina — a 10–15 minute waterfront walk from Expedia's 40-acre campus. Phase 2 adds a direct Bainbridge ↔ Elliott Bay Marina overlay with no downtown transfer, and revives the Des Moines ↔ Bell Harbor run that a 2022 passenger-ferry pilot already proved marina-to-marina. Later phases explore Kingston, Edmonds, and a Gig Harbor ↔ Tacoma shuttle. We serve landings the public ferries don't — as a complement to the region's ferry system, never a replacement.

decision_ledger.topic: South Lake Union landings (Lake Union Park / Historic Ships Wharf, Chandler's Cove / Lake Union Piers, AGC Marina)
decision_ledger.status: real docks, dead corridor — inventoried, NOT routed
decision_ledger.reason: Speed-stranded — reachable only through the blanket 7-kn Ship Canal system: ~4.3 nm ≈ 37 min slow transit from Webster Point before any open-lake leg (Kirkland↔SLU ≈ 50–55 min total, outside the 20–45 min sweet spot). Revisit ONLY if rule relief is ever obtained — SMC 16.20.130 has no exemption pathway short of a code amendment. Zero SLU stops in any phase; the SLU employer cluster (Amazon SLU, Google SLU, Fred Hutch, Gates Foundation) lives in internal notes only and is never rendered as a served anchor.

Pier 50's two slips are saturated with KCWT + Kitsap service (Kitsap is building a new Pier 46 terminal for exactly this reason) and Colman Dock is WSF's terminal. Navier's downtown landing is Bell Harbor Marina; Pier 50 and Colman never render as Navier stations.

Distance/vessel class outside the 20–45 min sweet spot (Tacoma↔Seattle ≈ 60 min, needs a larger vessel per the PSRC record). Gig Harbor↔Tacoma is authored instead as its own Phase-3 Narrows sub-network with no Seattle link.

First-come queue-based lockage (~10–15 min cycles best case, 1–4 hr waits documented), 4-kn approach zones, and the blanket 7-kn Ship Canal on the lake side. Not commuter-schedulable; the two clusters are permanently independent networks.
